health.gc: Two explicit GC calls with event-loop turns; no heap/CPU profiler
health.cache: Imported modules/gRPC channel/allocator warmed by declared requests; no prepared HTML cache
health.memoryScope: Frontend process only; RSS includes native/allocator/socket memory; heapUsed is idle post-GC JS heap, not leak proof. Checkpoint administration allocations are included.
health.maxActiveScope: Cumulative process lifetime, not reset per wave

methodology: Separate explicit-GC retention diagnostic, no CPU ranks. Complete responses validate token, every field and completion; paused-abort responses deliberately do not claim full output validation. Admissions use batches no larger than declared concurrency. Every batch waits exact admissions/terminal counters and active=0 before next batch, and verifies cumulative observed server maxActive<=concurrency. Client cancellation does not free a server admission slot early. Batch outcomes/counters retained including failures. Server terminal counters report completed-before-abort versus cancelled; all waves settle active=0 before idle GC. Sequential lane/size cases share a warmed process, not independent process baselines; complete and abort waves alternate and influence later checkpoints. Fetch pool and gRPC/modules warm explicitly; slow clients use unpooled sockets. Frontend post-GC JS heap vs RSS/native/external memory kept distinct. Every sample and failure retained; slope descriptive only, no proof of all leaks or application-wide concurrency limits.
